claims.text: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts use relatively high platinum-group-metal loadings on traditional oxide supports.
A high-entropy oxide support can stabilize isolated, single-atom Pt-group-metal sites.
The proposed benefits will hold under high-temperature, oxygen-rich automotive exhaust conditions and extended operation.
Randomly mixed transition metals in a high-entropy oxide create high configurational disorder.
The high-entropy oxide matrix creates abundant oxygen vacancies.
Configurational disorder and oxygen vacancies stabilize atomically dispersed Pd or Pt sites.
Atomic-level noble-metal dispersion minimizes aggregation, which is a catalyst degradation pathway.
A high-entropy oxide support tailors adsorbate binding energies relevant to CO oxidation.
The high-entropy oxide/Pt-group-metal interaction enhances redox cycling.
The support increases tolerance to thermal and chemical stress.
Improved noble-metal utilization reduces the amount of platinum-group metal required.
The modified catalyst will have a lower CO oxidation light-off temperature than a conventional oxide-supported catalyst.
The modified catalyst will have better long-term stability than a conventional oxide-supported catalyst.
The modified catalyst will provide similar or better catalytic performance at a lower platinum-group-metal loading.
Traditional oxide-supported automotive catalysts typically have higher CO light-off temperatures than the proposed catalyst.
Traditional oxide-supported automotive catalysts deactivate faster over time than the proposed catalyst.
Effectiveness may depend on synthesis reproducibility, support compositional uniformity, and stability in realistic operating environments.

contradictions.description: The baseline and predicted outcome require demonstrating performance at lower PGM loading than a higher-loaded conventional catalyst, but the stated experiment prepares the two catalyst sets with equivalent PGM loading. The design therefore does not directly implement the lower-loading comparison invoked by the falsification rule.
